---
title: "S3 - Supply model and variants"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("R/00_utils/notebook_setup.R")
```

**Stage:** S3 (supply).
**Purpose:** convert observed river flow into a firm abstraction rate over the
command area and express it in claims/day, capped by infrastructure.
**Inputs:** `output/catchment_table.csv`, raw streamflow via `io.R`.
**Outputs:** none (worked example + assertions).
**Parameters:** `P$s_firm = 0.5`, `P$cap_mm = 10`, `P$eco_frac = 0.10`,
`P$d_mm`.

## Equations

```
S_raw(t) = Q(t) * 86400 * s_firm           [m^3/day]
S_mm(t)  = S_raw(t) / A_cmd * 1000         [mm/day]
mu(t)    = min(S_mm(t), cap_mm) / d        [claims/day]
```

Three predeclared variants:

- **SUP-1** firm share of observed flow (primary), capped at `cap_mm`.
- **SUP-2** dependable flow: flow clipped at its 5th percentile, then capped.
- **SUP-3** infrastructure-first: full `cap_mm` whenever flow is above an
  ecological floor, otherwise SUP-1.

## Worked example

```{r}
ct <- nb_require("catchment_table.csv", "S3")
g <- ct$gauge_id[1]
cr <- ct[gauge_id == g]
fl <- read_camels_flow(g)[, c("date", as.character(g))]
q <- fl[[as.character(g)]]

s1 <- rep(NA_real_, length(q))
s2 <- rep(NA_real_, length(q))
s3 <- rep(NA_real_, length(q))
ok <- !is.na(q)
s1[ok] <- supply_mm_day(q[ok], cr$area_cmd_m2, P$s_firm, P$cap_mm)
q_dep <- quantile(q, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
s2[ok] <- pmin(q_m3s_to_mm_day(pmin(q[ok], q_dep), cr$area_cmd_m2), P$cap_mm)
q_eco <- P$eco_frac * mean(q, na.rm = TRUE)
s3[ok] <- ifelse(q[ok] >= q_eco, P$cap_mm,
                 supply_mm_day(q[ok], cr$area_cmd_m2, P$s_firm, P$cap_mm))
mu1 <- s1 / P$d_mm; mu2 <- s2 / P$d_mm; mu3 <- s3 / P$d_mm

nb_assert(all(mu1 >= 0, na.rm = TRUE), "negative SUP-1 supply")
nb_assert(all(mu1 <= P$cap_mm / P$d_mm + 1e-12, na.rm = TRUE),
          "SUP-1 exceeds the infrastructure cap")
nb_assert(all(abs(mu1 - s1 / P$d_mm) < 1e-12, na.rm = TRUE),
          "mu must equal S_mm / d")
```

```{r fig-supply}
dt <- data.table(
  variant = rep(c("SUP-1", "SUP-2", "SUP-3"), each = length(q)),
  mu = c(mu1, mu2, mu3)
)[is.finite(mu)]
ggplot(dt, aes(mu, fill = variant)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, colour = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~variant, ncol = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#0072B2", "#E69F00", "#009E73"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "supply (claims/day)", y = "days",
       title = sprintf("Gauge %d: supply distributions by variant", g)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)
```

`[measurement]` The cap binds on high-flow days, so supply saturates at
`cap_mm/d = 0.5` claims/day. This is what keeps utilisation `rho` in a
physically meaningful range instead of collapsing to zero.
